is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles coluzzii (page 1, abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (1014F), Vgsc L995S (1014S), Vgsc N1570Y (1575Y), and Ace-1 G280S (119S) (page 10, section 3.9 and 3.10).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table S6 and the text provide genotype counts for 1014F, 1014S, and 1575Y (page 10, section 3.9).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in Gounougou, northern Cameroon (page 2, section 2.1).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an original research article (page 1).

sub_country_location.evidence: Gounougou, northern Cameroon (9°03′00″ N, 13°43′59″ E) (page 2, section 2.1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collection was carried out in August 2019 (page 2, section 2.1).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper states this collection was made 24 months after a previous collection in 2017 (Fadel et al., 2019), but this is a new, distinct collection event.

supplement.evidence: The required genotype data is provided in the text and Table S6 (which is part of the provided document).

assessment.summary: This study investigates pyrethroid resistance intensity and molecular mechanisms in Anopheles coluzzii from Gounougou, Cameroon. It uses bioassays, RNA-seq, and genotyping of kdr and ace-1 mutations. High pyrethroid resistance was observed, with metabolic resistance (GSTe2, P450s) identified as a key driver, while kdr mutations showed decreased frequencies compared to 2017.
